title: Opponent quotes Le Blanc's Thesis I listing Rome's four imputed calumnies on justification
source_text: CXXIX. Atque ut criminis illius me convincat, profert primam Thesium illarum quas vellicandas sibi proposuit. Verba Theseos sunt, Inter varias calumnias quibus Protestantium Doctrina in Justificationis negotio impetitur, hae quoque frequenter occurrunt. Quod communi consensu doceant, omnes & singulos Homines posse & debere certa fide credere sibi fuisse remissa peccata, & se coram Deo justos esse. Id illis tam firmiter persuasum esse debere, quam hoc, Jesum Christum esse Dei filium & Mundi Redemptorem, & similia fidei dogmata. Talem persuasionem ita necessariam esse, ut absque ea nemo vere fidelis & justus esse possit, non secus ac si credere detrectaret aliquem ex praecipuis & fundamentalibus fidei articulis. In ejusmodi persuasione fidem veram & salvificam constituendam esse, tanquam in ejus actu proprio atque praecipuo: adeoque homines tali fide, & quidem sola, coram Deo justificari, licet alioqui vitiis indulgeant, nec studeant bonis operibus. Istud praesertim videre est apud Bellarminum & Becanum Jesuitas, qui talia vel supponunt, vel etiam expresse & diserte nobis affingunt, in suis contra nos disputationibus.
pass_a_gloss: And to convict me of that crime, he brings forward the first of those theses he proposed to himself to pluck at. The words of the Thesis are: Among the various calumnies with which the Protestants' Doctrine is attacked in the matter of Justification, these also frequently occur. That by common consent they teach that all and each persons can and ought by certain faith to believe their sins have been remitted to them, and that they are just before God. That this ought to be as firmly persuaded to them as this — that Jesus Christ is the Son of God and Redeemer of the World, and similar doctrines of faith. That such persuasion is so necessary that without it no one can be truly faithful and just, no differently than if he refused to believe some one of the chief and fundamental articles of faith. That in such persuasion true and saving faith is to be constituted, as in its proper and chief act: and so people are justified before God by such faith, and by it alone, even if otherwise they indulge vices and do not pursue good works. This is especially to be seen in Bellarmine and Becanus the Jesuits, who either suppose such things or even expressly and clearly fasten them on us in their disputations against us.
pass_b_english: To convict Le Blanc, the opponent cites Thesis I's list of calumnies Rome often pins on Protestants regarding justification:
(1) all persons can/ought by certain faith believe their sins remitted and themselves just before God;
(2) with the same firmness as believing Christ is God's Son and world's Redeemer;
(3) such persuasion so necessary that without it none is truly faithful/just;
(4) true saving faith consists in that persuasion as its proper chief act — justifying even the vicious without good works.
Le Blanc names Bellarmine and Becanus as sources who suppose or expressly fasten these on the Reformed.

lemmas.gloss: expressly and clearly fasten on us

choices.english: calumnies with which the Doctrine is attacked
choices.why: Thesis I frame: imputed, not confessed, Reformed teaching.
rejected: these four as Le Blanc's own positive doctrine
